task_instance: Create a custom React Flow node component ('VideoNode') with TypeScript types, Handle/NodeResizer usage, and Zustand store integration, following the skill's Node Component Pattern and Type Definition Pattern (the skill's assets/ template files referenced in SKILL.md were not present in this repo checkout, so the component was written directly from the patterns documented inline in SKILL.md). Verified by type-checking with tsc and by rendering the component to static HTML with react-dom/server.
evidence: Set up a minimal TS project in the work dir with `npm install reactflow zustand react react-dom` and `-D typescript @types/react @types/react-dom esbuild`. Created src/types/index.ts (VideoNodeData interface extending Record<string, unknown> and VideoNode = Node<VideoNodeData,'video-node'>), src/store/app-store.ts (zustand useAppStore with updateNode/canvasMode per the skill pattern), src/components/nodes/VideoNode.tsx (memo-wrapped component using NodeResizer, target/source Handle, useAppStore selectors, exactly mirroring the skill's 'Node Component Pattern' code block), src/components/nodes/index.ts (export), and src/components/Canvas.tsx (registers 'video-node' in ReactFlow nodeTypes and renders an initial node), matching the skill's 6-step Integration Steps. Ran `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` -> exit 0 (no type errors) after fixing one real-world type gap: reactflow v11's NodeProps<T> does not include width/height even though Node<T> does, so VideoNodeProps was extended with `width?: number | null; height?: number | null;` to match the skill's example signature. Then wrote src/render-test.tsx which renders <VideoNode/> via react-dom/server's renderToStaticMarkup with full required NodeProps, bundled it with `npx esbuild src/render-test.tsx --bundle --platform=node --format=cjs --jsx=automatic --outfile=dist-test.cjs`, and ran `node dist-test.cjs`, which printed the rendered HTML containing the node title ('Intro clip'), the description paragraph, and both react-flow__handle-top (target) and react-flow__handle-bottom (source) elements, then printed RENDER_CHECK_OK (exit 0). This confirms the generated component is valid TypeScript, matches the skill's documented patterns and integration steps, and actually renders correctly with React Flow's runtime.
